title: Comparative Study of Tungsten Carbide Bonded with Equiatomic Cantor Alloy CoCrFeMnNi Sintered Conventionally and Spark Plasma
content: Cemented carbides consist of a hard phase (WC) and a binder (Co), which together provide excellent properties such as high hardness, resistance to fracture and wear, and corrosion resistance superior to steel and other metals used in engineering. Cobalt is the most commonly used binder; its function is to join the carbide particles and provide higher toughness and wear resistance [1]. Cemented carbides are generally produced via powder metallurgy, a process that involves compacting the material followed by sintering process. Several sintering techniques exist, like hot isostatic pressing (HIP), spark plasma sintering (SPS), vacuum hot pressing (VHP), and conventional sintering (CS) [1]. On the other hand, high entropy alloys (HEAs) are composed of five or more metallic elements in equiatomic or near-equiatomic proportions, and they present excellent mechanical properties due to their high thermodynamic stability. The CoCrFeMnNi system is the most studied HEA due its physical properties. The crystal structure consists of a single FCC solid solution, which makes it an ideal binder since FCC structures are typically very ductile [2]. This work focuses on evaluating the microstructure and mechanical properties of cemented carbides in which the high entropy alloy (CoCrFeMnNi) is incorporated as a binder substitute for cobalt, using two different sintering methods: conventional sintering (CS) and spark plasma sintering (SPS).
